decisions.reason: The paper explicitly replicates the ADOS domain CSS calibration study for Modules 1-3 by Hus, Gotham, & Lord (2014) (DOI: 10.1007/s10803-012-1719-1, listed in References at line 815), testing 8 of its 12 age/language cells in the SSC sample. The shipped row mispaired this citation with a same-year sibling paper on ADOS Module 4 by Hus & Lord (2014) (DOI: 10.1007/s10803-014-2080-3), which is mentioned only once in passing in the Discussion (line 668) as background context and is not tested.

After resolving the dependent original identity for row 412 to Hus, Gotham, & Lord (2014) (10.1007/s10803-012-1719-1, blind target_index 0), the authors state an explicit overall replication verdict confirming that the ADOS domain calibrated severity scores effectively reduced associations with non-ASD child characteristics (age and cognitive/developmental level) compared to raw domain totals in the independent SSC sample. Both shipped and blind correctly code the outcome as successful.

decisions.quote: Using a sample of 2,509 probands with ASD from the Simons Simplex Collection (SSC), this study provides the first replication of the ADOS domain CSS in an independent sample. Consistent with the original standardization study, when applied to existing SSC data, the ADOS domain CSS were less influenced by age and cognitive ability compared to raw domain totals.
decisions.reason: The study evaluates the published ADOS domain CSS calibration findings of Hus, Gotham, & Lord (2014) in an independent sample of 2,509 children from the Simons Simplex Collection rather than re-analyzing the original calibration dataset. Both shipped and blind correctly classify the record type as replication.

raw_expert_opinion.location: Scientific Abstract (lines 48-50); Introduction (lines 114-131); Method (lines 138-140, 262-274); Discussion (lines 638-641); References (line 815)
raw_expert_opinion.reason: The primary study empirically retests the ADOS domain calibrated severity scores (SA-CSS and RRB-CSS) in an independent sample of 2,509 children with ASD aged 4-16 across ADOS Modules 1, 2, and 3 in the Simons Simplex Collection, testing whether SA-CSS and RRB-CSS significantly reduce associations with child age and cognitive ability compared to raw domain totals as originally reported by Hus, Gotham, and Lord (2014). The reference list (line 815) explicitly identifies 'Hus V, Gotham K, Lord C. Standardizing ADOS Domain Scores: Separating Severity of Social Affect and Restricted and Repetitive Behaviors. Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders. 2014;44(10):2400–2412. doi: 10.1007/s10803-012-1719-1', matching Crossref metadata. The only shipped row, row 412 (10.1007/s10803-014-2080-3; Vanessa Hus & Catherine Lord, 2014, 'The Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule, Module 4: Revised Algorithm and Standardized Severity Scores', Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders 44(8):1996-2012), is a different two-author paper that develops the revised algorithm and severity scores specifically for Module 4 (older adolescents and adults), whereas the present replication excludes Module 4 and retests only the Modules 1-3 domain calibrations from Hus, Gotham, and Lord (2014) (10.1007/s10803-012-1719-1). Thus report equivalence does not apply and 10.1007/s10803-012-1719-1 is genuinely absent. No prior adjudication or state files exist.
